name: Helmuth von Moltke the Elder

roles.title: Chief of the Prussian (from 1871 the Great) General Staff

summary: Chief of the General Staff for thirty years and the victor of 1864, 1866 and 1870 — the man who made the Prussian staff, the railway timetable and the mobilization plan into instruments of war. Two inheritances run from him into 1914: the two-front problem, which he answered with a defensive war in the west and limited offensives in the east rather than a knock-out blow, and the warning that no plan of operations survives the first encounter with the enemy's main body — the sentence the campaign that followed is measured against. Uncle of the younger Moltke who directed it.
